Good — CPython's strict csv raises on `"a"b` patterns and unclosed quotes ✓, and treats bare quotes inside unquoted fields as literals ✓. My implementation delegates to csv.reader ✓ so it matches the reference semantics exactly.

Now let me fix the test file accordingly.

cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
src=open('tmp/t_capture.py').read()
src=src.replace("""# window 128 MiB exactly is accepted; larger is not
plain=zstd.ZstdCompressionParameters.from_level(1,window_log=27,write_content_size=1)
wf=zstd.ZstdCompressor(compression_params=plain).compress((HEADER+'\\r\\n').encode())
j['captures'][0]['chunks']=[base64.b64encode(wf).decode()]
if run(j).get('error'): print('FAIL window 128MiB rejected',run(j)); ok=False
params=zstd.ZstdCompressionParameters.from_level(1,window_log=28,write_content_size=1)
wf=zstd.ZstdCompressor(compression_params=params).compress((HEADER+'\\r\\n').encode())
j['captures'][0]['chunks']=[base64.b64encode(wf).decode()]
ok&=expect('window too big',run(j),'capture')""",
"""# window 128 MiB exactly is accepted; larger is not
import struct
def raw_frame(descriptor,payload=(HEADER+'\\r\\n').encode()):
    head=(len(payload)<<3)|1
    return (b'\\x28\\xb5\\x2f\\xfd'+b'\\x00'+bytes([descriptor])
            +struct.pack('<I',head)[:3]+payload)
j['captures'][0]['chunks']=[base64.b64encode(raw_frame(0x88)).decode()]
if run(j).get('error'): print('FAIL window 128MiB rejected',run(j)); ok=False
j['captures'][0]['chunks']=[base64.b64encode(raw_frame(0x90)).decode()]
ok&=expect('window 256MiB',run(j),'capture')
j['captures'][0]['chunks']=[base64.b64encode(raw_frame(0xf8)).decode()]
ok&=expect('window huge',run(j),'capture')""")
